prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the conception and first demonstration of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, in which bifunctional small molecules direct a ubiquitin ligase to destroy a chosen protein

statement.case_for: I keep the same configuration after reading all eight round-1 files. Each part has a principle that can be said in one sentence and opens a capability that did not exist before. Base editing converts one nucleobase to another by deamination directed to a chosen site, with no double-strand break, and it has been reproduced widely, in animals and in early human trials. Targeted protein degradation replaces occupancy-driven inhibition with event-driven removal by recruiting an E3 ligase, and independent groups have confirmed that on many targets. The two parts are non-overlapping, they cover nucleic-acid chemistry and protein homeostasis, and the names stay at three: Liu alone, and Crews with Deshaies, who conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional degrader in 2001. Four members now include B029 and four include B018, and I am not treating those counts as an argument. What persuades me is that the round-1 exchange narrowed the attribution questions in both parts, and neither part needs more than three names to be stated honestly.
statement.case_against: Both parts are chemical biology with a medicine flavour, and neither has an approved drug behind it that I can confirm, so the committee could be accused of rewarding promise over delivered outcome. Base editing follows the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize, and Somfai and Sparr are right that it is an engineered fusion on a platform that prize recognised. The cap of three names leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida, Kondo, Ciulli, Sakamoto, Handa and Ito, and that is a real cost, in particular Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands made degraders a rational chemical series. If the committee wanted a single, mature, unambiguously chemical achievement, B002 would be easier to defend than my second part.

responses.point: Base editing should not stand alone four to six years after the 2020 genome-editing prize and should be paired with a mature method such as Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling, which has the cleanest attribution and 25 years of confirmation.
responses.response: I accept the risk that a base-editing-led prize reads as a second genome-editing award, and that is why I do not hold B029 alone. I do not follow your conclusion that the partner should be B002. You have not yet stated the principle beyond ligand optimisation, and the Kosugi precedent and the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize both sit behind it. Maturity alone is not the criterion I apply. A prize that says what is new in chemistry should carry a partner that is also new. That is why I still prefer B018, whose principle, event-driven pharmacology through induced proximity, is not an extension of anything recognised before. I keep B002 as my first alternative and would move to it if you or Zou can state the new catalytic principle in one sentence, but nothing in round 1 has done that.

responses.point: A degradation prize should name Crews, Deshaies and Handa so that three people span both the PROTAC and the cereblon molecular-glue strands, with Ciulli as the possible swap for Handa.
responses.response: I share your reading of the science and I take your point that Handa's identification of cereblon unifies the glue strand. I still keep him out. The cereblon and thalidomide story is a mechanism-of-action discovery on a drug already in use, and the citation would then cover two achievements, which Brzezinski also says forces an arbitrary split. A Crews and Deshaies citation worded around the heterobifunctional concept is a single story I can explain to a broad audience, and it uses two of my three name slots, so Liu stays in. I agree with you and Sparr that Ciulli is the weakest exclusion. If the committee decides the PROTAC part needs a third name, I would take Ciulli before Handa, but I would not give up the second part to do it.

responses.point: Base editing is an engineering fusion of a deaminase onto the nickase platform recognised in 2020, and Nishida and Kondo's Target-AID work means a Liu-only citation is not as safe as it looks.
responses.response: The objection about the platform is fair, and I have weighed it. My answer is that what is new is not the nickase but the chemistry performed on the base. An evolved deaminase carries out a defined reaction on one nucleotide in a living cell, with product purity and a window set by the editor design, and that is a chemical advance and not only a delivery of Cas9. On Target-AID I think the citation can be limited to the engineered base editor concept and its directed evolution, in which Liu's group made the cytosine and adenine editors. Nishida and Kondo are a parallel claim that I acknowledge and cannot dismiss, but I would put them in the background text, as the committee did with prior work in earlier years, not as a reason to withdraw Liu. I would keep prime editing outside the citation.

responses.point: Base editing is hydrolytic deamination engineered by directed evolution and transparent in enzymology, so a Liu-only part is defensible, and a PROTAC part with Crews and Deshaies can carry a clean citation.
responses.response: We are in the same configuration and I want to test it rather than rest on it. You list Handa's cereblon work as a real attribution cost. I do not disagree, and I think the right way to carry it is in the wording of the citation, which should name the bifunctional concept and leave glue degraders to a later cycle. I also share your concern about the absence of an approved PROTAC drug. For my own decision I would say that independent confirmation of the mechanism on many targets and a deep clinical pipeline together outweigh a missing approval, but a first approval or a clear failure in late trials would change my ranking of B018 relative to B002 and B016.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes B018 premature compared with B002 or B016, and whether regulatory approval should be an explicit threshold.
Whether the Target-AID priority of Nishida and Kondo is strong enough to change a Liu-only citation, or can be handled in background text.
Whether a PROTAC citation limited to Crews and Deshaies is stable, given Ciulli, Sakamoto and Handa, or whether the committee will insist on a third name.

Whether two chemical-biology parts is the right balance, or the committee should prefer a mature core-chemistry achievement such as B002, for which nobody has yet stated what is new beyond the 2010 prize.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name. I share a Lund affiliation with committee colleagues Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr, but no candidate on the shortlist is connected to Lund or to me personally. My own research is on molecular motors and nanodevices and is not connected to base editing or targeted protein degradation.
